s: Righteousness is described as the ritual truth pursued by the saints. Ahura Mazda's Fravashi attains its ends most because of Righteousness.

l: Gaya Maretan (the life-man), Yasna, Yasna XXVI.
s: Gaya Maretan is identified as holy and as the first created. His Fravashi is worshipped, and he marks the beginning of the succession extending to Saoshyant.
Zarathustra Spitâma is identified as a saint. His sanctity and Fravashi are worshipped.
Saoshyant is identified as the victorious. The Fravashis of the saints are worshipped from Gaya Maretan to Saoshyant.

The souls of holy men and women, including the dead, living, and unborn, are worshipped. The unit also worships the soul of the Kine of blessed gift and the souls of the dead who are identified as the Fravashis of the saints.

This unit concerns the worship and furtherance of Ahura Mazda, the greatest lord and master, and the smiting of Angra Mainyu, Aêshma, and wicked Daêvas. It presents the Ahuna-vairya as a sacred gift and recital that offers saving wisdom and worship. It also declares that the Kingdom belongs to Ahura and concludes by worshipping the Ahuna-vairya and Asha Vahista.

Ahura Mazda is rendered as the greatest lord and master, and the unit seeks to further Him through worship. His Kingdom is declared to belong to Him, and He is asked how one may serve Him by nourishing the poor.
The Ahuna-vairya is intoned with sanctity as a sacred gift offering saving acts of wisdom and worship. It is worshipped at the close of the unit.

l: Righteousness the Best, Yasna, Yasna XXVII.
s: Asha Vahista is invoked among the Lords and is worshipped at the close of the unit as the most beautiful Bountiful Immortal.

Yasna XXVIII consists of prayers chiefly for grace and the words of revelation. Zarathustra addresses Ahura Mazda, Righteousness, Good Mind, and Piety, seeking spiritual gifts, understanding, long-lasting life, and power to overcome torment. The prayers concern both corporeal and mental worlds, the Soul of the Kine, and the advancement of the imperishable Kingdom. Zarathustra also asks to be taught how the primeval world arose so he may declare it to the waiting people.

l: Yasna XXVIII, Yasna, Yasna / Yasna XXVIII.
s: Yasna XXVIII contains prayers chiefly for grace and the words of revelation. It presents supplications for Righteousness, Good Mind, spiritual attainments, long-lasting life, and understanding of how the primeval world arose.

Zarathustra offers prayers and teaches the people concerning holy deeds performed with faith toward God and in desire for Righteousness. He asks for spiritual help, long-lasting life, and instruction from Ahura Mazda so that he may declare it to the waiting people.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna / Yasna XXVIII.
s: Ahura Mazda is addressed as the Great Creator and Living Lord, and is asked to grant grace, understanding, spiritual attainments, long-lasting life, and powerful help. He is also asked to teach Zarathustra how the primeval world arose.

l: Good Mind, Yasna, Yasna / Yasna XXVIII.
s: Good Mind is sought for understanding, spiritual attainments, and the advancement of the imperishable Kingdom. It is associated with Benevolent Mind, the rewards of Righteousness, and the ages of divine benevolence.

Righteousness is invoked as a divine power through which actions are performed, gifts are bestowed, and recipients are introduced into beatitude and glory. It is asked to grant sacred blessing and to help hold off spiritual foulness.

The prayers seek gracious help, understanding, spiritual gifts, long-lasting life, protection, and the power to overcome torment. They are offered to Ahura Mazda and the divine qualities, and include requests on behalf of Zarathustra, Vîstâspa, Frashaostra, and the people.

The Soul of the Kine cries to Ahura and Asha about violence, desolation, and the lack of a capable guardian and pasture-giver. Ahura asks Asha who was appointed to protect the Kine, and Asha answers that no suitable chieftain could be found. Zarathustra intervenes, and Ahura names Zarathustra Spitama as the spiritual master and speaker for the diligent tiller of the ground. The unit asks Ahura, Asha, Good Mind, and Sovereign Power to grant aid, protection, gladness, and peaceful homes to the righteous and their disciples.

Ahura is addressed by the Soul of the Kine for help and is asked about the Kine's guardian. He is described as the discerning arbiter and as understanding mysterious grace. Ahura names Zarathustra Spitama as a spiritual master and speaker, and is asked to grant aid and peaceful happiness.
Asha is addressed by Ahura about the guardian appointed for the Kine. Asha answers that a chieftain able to repel the fury of the wicked and free from hate could not be obtained.

l: Soul of the Kine, Yasna, Yasna XXIX.
s: The Soul of the Kine cries aloud about assault, violent power, desolation, insolence, and thievish might. It has no pasture-giver other than Ahura and Asha, later laments that its lord is powerless, and asks when strong-handed help will appear.
The Kine are described as holy herds whose Soul seeks protection, good tillage, pasture, food, and a capable guardian. Their condition includes wounding and exposure to fearful ravages.
Zarathustra Spitama is the one who has hearkened to Ahura's and Asha's enunciations. He desires to proclaim their mighty acts of grace and is named as a spiritual master and authoritative speaker.

l: the tiller of the earth, Yasna, Yasna XXIX.
s: The diligent tiller of the earth is identified as the one for whom Ahura names Zarathustra as a spiritual master. The righteous and thrifty tiller is distinguished from the wicked and is not to suffer destruction with them.

A chieftain is sought as a skilled, energetic guardian of the Kine who can repel the fury of the wicked. Asha says that no chieftain possessing the required power and freedom from hate could be found.
The Good Mind is associated with Ahura's Sovereign Kingdom and with the doctrines given to mortals. It is also invoked as a source of strength for Zarathustra's task and mission.
The Sovereign Kingdom is requested from Ahura and Asha for the disciples. Through the Good Mind, it bestows peaceful home life and quiet happiness against fearful ravages.

The Doctrine of Dualism concerns the choice between two primeval spirits, one better and one worse, in thought, word, and deed. It teaches that the better spirit chose Righteousness, while the worse spirit chose evil, and that the Demon-gods chose the Worst Mind and allied themselves with the Demon of Fury. Ahura Mazda, the Good Mind, Righteousness, Âramaiti, and the Sovereign Power oppose falsehood and work toward the perfection of the world. The unit promises Heaven and salvation for the righteous and Hell and the worst life for the wicked.

l: The Doctrine of Dualism, Yasna, Yasna XXX.
s: It teaches about two primeval spirits and the choice between better and worse thought, word, and deed. It calls hearers to decide rightly between religions and to join the work of the great renovation.
Ahura Mazda is praised and addressed as the living Lord. His Kingdom is to be gained through the Good Mind, and the righteous are to gather in His happy abode.

The Good Mind inspires sacrifices and is associated with Righteousness. It helps gain the Kingdom for Ahura and commands those who will deliver the Demon of the Lie into the hands of the Righteous Order.
Righteousness is praised and chosen by the better spirit. It works with Âramaiti, the Good Mind, and the Sovereign Power, and will receive the Demon of the Lie as a captive.

l: two first spirits, Yasna, Yasna XXX.
s: The primeval spirits are a pair, independent in action and opposed as better and worse in thought, word, and deed. They came together to determine life, its absence, and the world's final ordering.

l: more bountiful spirit, Yasna, Yasna XXX.
s: The better spirit chose Righteousness and chose those who content Ahura with actions in accordance with the faith. It clothes itself with the firm stones of heaven as its robe.
The worse spirit chose evil and thereby worked the worst possible results. Its choice is associated with the worst life for the wicked.
The Demon-gods and their worshippers cannot make a righteous choice. They chose the Worst Mind after questioning and debating, and then rushed to the Demon of Fury.
The Worst Mind approached the Demon-gods so that it might be chosen. Their choice of it led them toward the Demon of Fury and the pollution of mortal lives.

l: Demon of Fury, Yasna, Yasna XXX.
s: The Demon-gods allied themselves with the Demon of Fury. Through this alliance they sought to pollute the lives of mortals.

Âramaiti, the personified Piety of the saints, approached with the Sovereign Power, the Good Mind, and the Righteous Order. She gave a body to the spiritual creations of good and evil and is associated with abiding and strenuous endurance.

l: Demon of the Lie, Yasna, Yasna XXX.
s: The Demon of the Lie is to be delivered into the two hands of the Righteous Order. At the perfection of the world, destruction will fall upon it and its adherents.
It is urged to hear, observe, awaken to the teaching, and choose rightly between the two ways. It is also taught about the long wounding of the wicked and the blessings of the righteous.
The righteous saints will gather in the happy abode of the Good Mind and Ahura when perfection is attained. They are described as proceeding on earth in good repute and honour.
The wicked are assigned the worst life, and a long wounding is said to be in store for them. Their fate contrasts with the blessings and salvation promised to the righteous.

The world is to be ordered at the last, and the great renovation is to make it progressive until perfection is reached. At that time destruction will fall upon the Demon of Falsehood and its adherents.
Heaven is associated with the best mental state for the holy. The better spirit clothes itself with the firm stones of heaven as its robe.
Hell is identified with the worst life for the wicked. It stands in opposition to Heaven and the best mental state of the holy.
The two spirits determined life and life's absence when they first came together. The Demon-gods and the Demon of Fury sought to pollute the lives of mortals.
Religions are presented as matters for individual decision. The hearers are urged to listen and choose rightly between them.
The two spirits completed their respective parts in the deeds of creation and chose separate realms. Âramaiti gave a body to the spiritual creations of good and evil.
The great struggle began when the Daêvas first seized the Demon of Wrath as their ally. Its eventual just vengeance will accompany the gaining of the Kingdom for Ahura.
The great renovation is the work of those who make the world progressive until perfection is reached. Those who bring it on are urged to be like the Ahuras of Mazda in helpful readiness.

Salvation is promised when the foretold courses of punishment for the wicked and blessings for the righteous begin. The unit presents it as the portion of those who choose and follow the righteous way.

The unit concerns Ahura Mazda, the prophet, and the struggle between Righteousness and the Lie. It declares that Ahura Mazda reveals truth, appoints rule, supports the Good Mind and Righteous Order, and grants the Kingdom, Universal Weal, and Immortality to the faithful. It contrasts the husbandman, who chooses the good creed, with the thieving nomad, the wicked, and the evil-doer, whose actions bring ruin and punishment. It calls the living believers to hear the truthful teaching, reject harmful commands, and follow Righteous Order in thought, word, and deed.

Ahura Mazda reveals indubitable truths, appoints the ruler over the two struggling bands, and declares the vow and the truths that the living believers are to know. He creates and supports Righteous Order and the Good Mind, grants the Kingdom, Universal Weal, and Immortality, and rewards those who are His friends in spirit and deeds.

Righteous Order is the truth by which the living believers are to live and through which the better lot is given. It is created and sustained by Ahura Mazda, and those who follow it in words and actions become helpful and vigorous.
The Good Mind is given by Ahura Mazda and works within the faithful. It helps them know the truth, follow Righteous Order, and serve the holy Kingdom through wise thoughts, words, and actions.
The Lie opposes Righteousness and delivers its settlements to death. Its harmful doctrines are followed by those who reject the truthful teaching, and its demon is to be smitten by the holy Kingdom.

l: the cause of Righteousness, Yasna, Yasna XXXI.
s: The cause of Righteousness is advanced through the declaration of doctrines and the faithful pursuit of truth. It is opposed by the Lie and is strengthened when the living believers follow Ahura Mazda's order.

l: the living believers, Yasna, Yasna XXXI.
s: The living believers are urged to hear Ahura Mazda's truthful teaching, reject the sinner's command, and follow Righteous Order. They are to use the Good Mind in their words and actions and fulfill their vows with faith.

l: the two struggling bands, Yasna, Yasna XXXI.
s: The two struggling bands receive a deciding satisfaction through Ahura Mazda's Spirit, Fire, and Righteousness. Ahura Mazda appoints a ruler over both so that they may live according to Righteousness.
The Kingdom is requested as a mighty power by which the Lie-demon may be smitten. Ahura Mazda gives its headship and vigorous might to those who follow Righteous Order and serve Him faithfully.

Piety belongs to Ahura Mazda and is active with the Good Mind in the faithful. It questions the two spirits and seeks understanding concerning future events, prayers, offerings, awards, and the final state.

The Mãthra of Welfare and Immortality is the best word that the All-wise One declares. It proclaims beneficent power and is associated with a Realm that flourishes in holiness to the Great Creator's glory.

l: Universal Weal and Immortality, Yasna, Yasna XXXI.
s: Universal Weal and Immortality are given by Ahura Mazda in the fulness of Righteous Order. They are granted to those who are faithful to Him and follow His order.
The Kine receives a path from Ahura Mazda and chooses the husbandman, the thrifty toiler in the fields, as a holy master. Her choice excludes the thieving nomad from the good creed.

l: the zealous and thrifty husbandman, Yasna, Yasna XXXI.
s: The husbandman is the thrifty toiler in the fields whom the Kine chooses as a holy master endowed with the Good Mind's wealth. He represents the one who follows the good creed and works within Righteous Order.

l: the thieving nomad, Yasna, Yasna XXXI.
s: The thieving nomad is rejected by the Kine's choice and shall not share the good creed. He is contrasted with the husbandman as one who does not receive the Kine's favor.

l: the settlements of Righteousness, Yasna, Yasna XXXI.
s: The settlements of Righteousness are delivered to death by those who follow the doctrinal vows of the harmful Lie. Ahura Mazda created the holy settlements and revealed religious laws for them.

The prophet declares the doctrines and truths concerning Ahura Mazda, Righteous Order, and the struggle with the Lie. He seeks Ahura Mazda's guidance so that he may make all the living believers understand the mighty truths.

The wicked receive an award associated with their actions and final state. Those who prepare the throne for the evil and cannot reclaim their lives except through lawless harm are questioned as coadjutors of the wicked.

The evil-doer is associated with preparing a throne for evil and with lawless harm to the tiller's herd and the pious husbandman's flock. The unit asks what award such a person receives and contrasts him with those who promote Ahura Mazda's holy Rule.

The unit concerns a rival-monarch and his allies, whose false religion, violence, and teachings threaten Zarathustra, his people, the Kine, and the doctrines of Ahura Mazda. Ahura Mazda answers through the Good Mind and Righteousness, accepting good Piety and condemning the Daêvas, Evil Mind, and Evil Spirit. The rival forces are associated with Grehma, the Karpans, and the Kavis, who oppose truth and damage life. Zarathustra declares that he will establish Ahura Mazda’s precepts and drive away the Karpans’ and Kavis’ disciples.

The rival-monarch is portrayed as seeking sovereignty in order to deliver homes, villages, towns, and provinces to ruin and death. He offers false religious devotions, destroys doctrines, perverts understanding, seizes wealth, rejects the Kine and the Sun, and attacks the saint.

Zarathustra prays to Ahura Mazda and seeks to hold back those who hate and offend Him. He distinguishes himself from the wretched beings, cries to Ahura Mazda and Righteousness for help, establishes Ahura Mazda’s precepts, and vows to drive away the Karpans’ and Kavis’ disciples.

Ahura Mazda answers through the Good Mind and Sovereign Power, accepting good Piety. He knows the true teachings, condemns the Daêvas and their allies, and possesses the power to heal Zarathustra’s woes and doubtings.
The Good Mind rules within the souls of those to whom Ahura Mazda answers. It is opposed by the Daêvas, the rival-monarch’s teachings, and those who are far astray from it.

Righteousness is associated with Ahura Mazda’s surpassing order and kingdom. Zarathustra seeks its aid, intends to establish Ahura Mazda’s precepts within it, and contrasts it with Grehma, the Karpans, and the Kavis.

The Daêvas are described as seeds from the Evil Mind and as false religious powers. Their worshippers are associated with the Lie-demon, deception, confusion, evil deeds, and separation from the Good Mind, Ahura Mazda, and Righteousness.
The Evil Mind is the source from which the Daêvas are said to come. It is linked with those who confuse thoughts, abandon the Good Mind, and become estranged from Ahura Mazda and Righteousness.
The Evil Spirit rules the Daêvas with an evil mind and an evil word directed toward action. Through them, he seeks to deprive mankind of happy life and Immortality.
Mankind is threatened with deception, loss of happy life on earth, and loss of Immortality. The rival forces and their teachings are said to confuse and beguile mankind.

Grehma is associated with those who love him above Righteousness and with the destroyers of life. He seeks these things through an evil kingdom, establishes the Kavis and their plans against Ahura Mazda, and is linked with attempts to conquer the Kine.
The Karpans are aligned with Grehma, the Kavis, and the Throne of those who desire the Demon of lies. Zarathustra says he will drive away the Karpans’ disciples.
The Kavis are established by Grehma and are associated with scheming plans and deceptive deeds that aid the wicked. Zarathustra says he will drive away their disciples.

The Kine are treated as sacred, but the rival leader declares them among the worst things visible and is said to destroy the Kine’s life. Grehma and his allies are associated with attempts to conquer or harm the Kine.

The rival leader is said to destroy and pervert the doctrines, while Zarathustra seeks to establish Ahura Mazda’s precepts. The condemned doctrines are connected with evil teachings, blasphemy, and rejection of the sacred Kine and the Sun.

Yasna XXXIII. concerns Zarathustra’s prayers and self-consecration to Ahura Mazda, seeking justice, guidance, power, and communion with the divine attributes. It rejects disobedience, the Evil Mind, arrogance, falsehood, and neglect of the Kine, while upholding the Righteous Order, Good Mind, Obedience, and Âramaiti. Zarathustra asks for insight, prosperity, salvation, and the gifts of Immortality and Welfare, and offers his body, speech, deeds, and spiritual priority to Mazda.
Yasna XXXIII. presents prayers, hopes, moral commitments, requests for divine guidance and power, and Zarathustra’s self-consecration.

Zarathustra is named by the Lord as the spiritual chieftain sought by the Kine. He abjures disobedience, the Evil Mind, arrogance, falsehood, and neglect of the Kine, seeks sight of and consultation with Ahura Mazda, and offers his body, Good Mind, Obedience, speech, and deeds.

Ahura Mazda is asked to grant justice, guidance, insight, power, strength, salvation, prosperity, Immortality, and Welfare. He is invoked as the divine authority with whom Zarathustra seeks consultation and communion.
Âramaiti is identified with piety and is asked to give Zarathustra power and to show forth religious truths through the Righteous Order.

The Righteous Order governs just action, provides straight paths, and is associated with Ahura Mazda’s dwelling. It is asked to reveal religious truths and to guide people toward the work-field of righteousness.

The Good Mind is associated with the pastures and Realm of Good Mind, divine instruction, salvation, and the fulfilment of worthy aims. Zarathustra seeks its guidance and offers it priority in his self-consecration.
The Evil Mind is among the faults that Zarathustra abjures.
Obedience is invoked as the greatest assisting guardian and is linked with long life in the Realm of Good Mind. Zarathustra offers his Obedience to Ahura Mazda in deed and speech.
Sovereign Power is invoked with the Good Mind and Sanctity as a means of salvation and is asked to grant Zarathustra power and strength.
The Kine seek a spiritual chieftain and are connected with the need for just leadership. Zarathustra abjures the worst care of the Kine’s meadows, described as stint in labour.
Religious faith receives offerings through opposition to evil and through good deeds, thoughts, words, labour, and admonition for another’s good.

l: Realm of Good Mind, Yasna, Yasna XXXIII.
s: The Realm of Good Mind is associated with long life and the manifestation of the Good Mind among the tribes.

l: offerings of worship, Yasna, Yasna XXXIII.
s: Offerings of worship are to become manifest among the worshippers, and Zarathustra asks for zeal and help in making them so.

The unit concerns Ahura Mazda, the gifts and powers associated with the Righteous Order, Good Mind, Âramaiti, and the Kingdom of Welfare, and the worship offered by faithful servants. It asks what Ahura Mazda’s Kingdom, riches, regulations, praise, and offerings are, and seeks signs, instruction, and protection through Righteousness. It describes sacrifice, prayer, Fire, and good actions as means of approaching Ahura Mazda and receiving blessed rewards. It also concerns the Kine, the settlements, the poor, and those who oppose or abandon the divine order.

Ahura Mazda is offered gifts, sacrifice, praise, and prayer in return for blessings. He is asked to reveal His regulations, teach the paths through Righteousness, protect the faithful, and grant signs and blessed rewards.
Immortality is one of the gifts given by Ahura Mazda through holy deeds, words, and sacrifice. Âramaiti increases it together with Universal Weal and the Righteous Order.
The Righteous Order is joined with Ahura Mazda’s gifts, Good Mind, Kingdom, and worship. It guides the paths of the saints, strengthens Fire, and is increased with Universal Weal and Immortality.

The Good Mind is associated with the gifts of Ahura Mazda and with the soul of the bountiful man. It protects settlements, produces doctrines, guides the faithful, and reveals the best words and actions.

The Kingdom of Welfare is one of the gifts given by Ahura Mazda through holy deeds, words, and sacrifice. Ahura Mazda’s Kingdom is sought as the sphere in which the Righteous Order, Good Mind, and Âramaiti establish welfare.

Âramaiti is described as bountiful Piety and as the creatrix of righteous beings. She departs from those who abandon her through evil and ignorance, and she increases Universal Weal, Immortality, and the Righteous Order.

l: the Universal Weal, Yasna, Yasna XXXIV.
s: Universal Weal is increased by Âramaiti together with Immortality and the Righteous Order. These lasting powers provide needed food and help remove hatred and foes.
The Fire of Ahura Mazda is strong through Righteousness, swift, and powerful. It brings joy and help to the house that receives it, while harming the hater as if struck by weapons.
The Kine is described as a mother whose toil is served by those who work for her. Their work furthers Ahura Mazda’s merciful care through understanding and the word of the Righteous Order.

Sacrifice is offered to Ahura Mazda, the Righteousness, and the settlements guarded by the Good Mind. Through sacrifice and praise, the worshipper seeks to approach Ahura Mazda and receive His rewards.

l: paths through Righteousness, Yasna, Yasna XXXIV.
s: The paths through Righteousness are requested from Ahura Mazda as the paths trodden by the Good Mind within the saints. They are connected with religious precepts and laws of the Saviours, through which the well-doer thrives.

l: sacred reward and blessing, Yasna, Yasna XXXIV.
s: Blessed rewards are established by Ahura Mazda’s ordinance and are associated with the path of the Good Mind and Righteousness. They are given for bodily life through the deeds of the Good Mind and are bestowed by Ahura Mazda.

Yasna XXXV., also called Yasna Haptanghâiti, praises Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Righteousness, and the Mazdayasnian Faith. It concerns the sacrifice and homage offered to the divine powers and to the entire clean, spiritual, and mundane creation. It calls for good thoughts, good words, and good actions, and for the care and comfort of the Kine. It also asks that the faith, its teachings, and its ritual order be proclaimed, practiced, and further diffused.

Yasna XXXV. praises Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Righteousness, and the Mazdayasnian Faith. It calls for their worship, for good thoughts, words, and actions, and for the practice and diffusion of the faith.
Yasna Haptanghâiti is another name given for Yasna XXXV. It is a prayer for the practice and diffusion of the faith.
Ahura Mazda is praised and worshipped as the holy Lord of the ritual order. He is asked to receive sacrifice and homage, to support the proclamation of righteous words, and to bestow further light.
The Bountiful Immortals are worshipped alongside Ahura Mazda. They are described as ruling and disposing of all things aright.
Righteousness is praised as beauteous and best. It is invoked with Ahura Mazda as the basis for choosing, proclaiming, and performing what is best.
The Mazdayasnian Faith is described as benignant. Its practice, teachings, and diffusion are among the purposes of the prayer.

The ritual order is associated with Ahura Mazda and provides shelter under which the worshippers should act. Its precepts are to be actively fulfilled toward the clean and better creatures fit to live.

The entire creation of the clean, the spiritual, and the mundane is included among those to whom sacrifice is offered. It is associated with the longing blessing of the beneficent ritual and the benignant Religion.
Good thoughts are praised together with good words and good actions, both those now and those hereafter. The worshippers choose to think them and to implant them with homage.
Good words are praised together with good thoughts and good actions. The worshippers choose to speak them and proclaim them as Righteousness and as belonging to the better mind.
Good actions are praised together with good thoughts and good words, both those now and those hereafter. The worshippers choose to perform them as the best for both worlds.
The Kine represents the pure creation and is the subject of prayer for comfort and fodder. The worshippers seek to nurture her and to act for her welfare.
Good Mind is invoked with Righteousness as a basis for the words and sayings the worshippers proclaim. The words are described as being of the better mind.
Yasna is presented as an instrument through which further spoken words and praises are offered. Through Yasna, the worshippers proclaim the teachings and ask Ahura Mazda to bestow their light.

This unit concerns Ahura Mazda and the Fire of Ahura Mazda. It asks for approach, aid, zeal, blessing, praise, and protection from pollution. It also acknowledges Ahura Mazda’s Good Mind, Righteousness, good wisdom, stars as His body, and the highest of the high.

Ahura Mazda is approached with prayers, confessions of guilt, good thoughts, well-said words, and well-done deeds. His Good Mind, Righteousness, and good wisdom are invoked, and acknowledgments are made to His most beauteous body and stars.

The Fire of Ahura Mazda is called the most bounteous one of His Spirit and possesses the most potent name for grace. It is asked to give zeal, approach, aid, and cover with pollutions whoever brings pollutions to it.
Zeal is requested from the Fire of Ahura Mazda as a friendly gift. It supports the greatest undertaking among the efforts described in the unit.
The Good Mind of Ahura Mazda is invoked as help for approaching Him.
Righteousness is invoked together with the Good Mind as a means of approaching Ahura Mazda.

l: stars (Ahura Mazda's body), Yasna, Yasna XXXVI.
s: The stars are identified as part of Ahura Mazda’s body. Deep acknowledgments are made to them.

The unit concerns worship of Ahura Mazda, the creator of the Kine (the living creation), Righteousness, waters, wholesome plants, stars, earth, and all good objects. Ahura Mazda is worshipped for His Sovereign Power, greatness, and beneficence, and under His name as Lord and Mazda dear. The Fravashis of the Just, Righteousness the Best, the Bountiful Immortals, the Good Mind, Good Faith, and Piety are also worshipped. The worship is offered with the body and life, and Righteousness is praised as beauteous and endowed with light in all things good.

Ahura Mazda is worshipped as the maker of the Kine (the living creation), Righteousness, the waters, wholesome plants, the stars, the earth, and all good objects. He is worshipped for His Sovereign Power, greatness, beneficence, and under His name as Lord and Mazda dear.
The Kine (the living creation) is described as made by Ahura Mazda. Ahura Mazda is worshipped as having priority among the Yazads who abide beside the Kine and care for her protection and support.

Righteousness is described as made by Ahura Mazda and as incarnate in the clean. Righteousness the Best is worshipped as the most beauteous, a Bountiful Immortal, and endowed with light in all things good.
Sovereign Power is associated with Ahura Mazda and is worshipped for its beneficence and greatness. It is also worshipped as belonging to the Lord.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Yasna, Yasna XXXVII.
s: The Fravashis of the Just are worshipped. The worship extends to the Fravashis of saints, holy men, and holy women.
The Bountiful Immortals are worshipped. Righteousness the Best is identified as a Bountiful Immortal.
The Good Mind of the Lord is worshipped.
Good Faith is worshipped as the good law of thrift.
Piety is worshipped as the ready mind within Thy folk.

This unit concerns worship of the earth, Ahura Mazda, and the waters. The earth is honored as the bearer of those who worship, together with the wives of Ahura Mazda, who are praised for their sanctity and pious qualities. The waters are worshipped in their various forms as beneficent, productive, maternal beings that serve, nourish, and aid people. Ahura Mazda is said to have given the waters their names when the good was bestowed.
The earth is worshipped as the one that bears those who worship, together with the wives of Ahura Mazda.

Ahura Mazda is addressed in worship, and His wives are worshipped for their sanctity and praised for their wise, pious, vigorous, blessed, and prosperous qualities. He is said to have given the beneficent waters their names when He who made the good bestowed them.

The waters are worshipped in forms that are showered down, stand in pools and vats, and bear forth vessels. They are called female Ahuras of Ahura, beneficent, productive, maternal, full-flowing, useful for bathing, nourishing to the frail and needy, and capable of reaching sickness or misfortune.

The unit concerns worship offered to the Kine's soul, her created body, cattle, tame and wild beasts, and the souls of saints. The saints are described as men and women whose good consciences have conquered, are conquering, or will conquer the Daêvas. The Bountiful Immortals, both male and female, are worshipped as ever-living and helpful beings dwelling beside the pious. Ahura Mazda is praised and worshipped for thinking, speaking, determining, and doing what is good, and prayers are directed to Him with confessions of sin.

l: Soul of the Kine, Yasna, Yasna XXXIX.
s: The Kine's soul is worshipped together with her created body. The souls of cattle fit to live are also worshipped.
The souls of saints, both men and women, are worshipped wherever they were born. Their good consciences have conquered, are conquering, or will conquer the Daêvas.
The Daêvas are opposed by the good consciences of the saints, which have conquered, are conquering, or will conquer them.
The Bountiful Immortals, both male and female, are worshipped. The males are described as ever living and ever helpful, dwelling beside the pious, and the females are described likewise.
Ahura Mazda is addressed as having thought, spoken, determined, and done what is good. He is offered worship, praise, reverence, and prayers with confessions of sin.

The unit consists of prayers addressed to Ahura Mazda for wise action, bounty, tenderness, and appointed reward. It asks for fellowship with Ahura Mazda and Righteousness for all duration. It requests righteous men, lovers and producers of the Right, and trained beasts for helpful companionship and enduring vigour. It also asks for a kinsman lord, labourers of the village, and clients or peers, through whose help the petitioners may arise and remain holy and true to Ahura Mazda.

Ahura Mazda is asked to act wisely with bounty and tenderness, grant appointed reward, provide righteous men and trained beasts, and establish helpful social relations. The petitioners seek to be holy and true to Ahura Mazda and to receive help through these provisions.

l: sacred reward and blessing, Yasna, Yasna XL.
s: Reward is described as appointed by Ahura Mazda for souls. It is requested for both this world and the spiritual.

l: fellowship with Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna XL.
s: Fellowship with Ahura Mazda is requested as part of what may be attained in this world and the spiritual.
Righteousness is requested alongside fellowship with Ahura Mazda for all duration.
Righteous men are requested from Ahura Mazda.

l: lovers and producers of the Right, Yasna, Yasna XL.
s: Lovers and producers of the Right are requested as men who are righteous.
The Right is associated with men who love and produce it.

l: tame and broken-in beasts, Yasna, Yasna XL.
s: Trained beasts are requested for the pastures, broken in for riding and bearing. They are to provide helpful companionship, long enduring vigour, and rejoicing grace.
A kinsman lord is requested for the petitioners, together with the labourers of the village.

l: labourers of the village, Yasna, Yasna XL.
s: The labourers of the village are requested to be associated with a kinsman lord.

l: clients or peers, Yasna, Yasna XL.
s: Clients or peers are requested to be present alongside the kinsman lord and the labourers of the village.

Yasna XLI. is a prayer praising Ahura Mazda and Righteousness the Best. It asks Ahura Mazda to rule benevolently, grant life, bodily vigor, power, salvation, and protection, and allow worshippers to attain his good Kingdom. It seeks long life and the reward appointed for souls, for both this life and that of mind. The unit concludes by offering sacrifice to Yasna Haptanghâiti as a brave, holy, and chief ritual.

Yasna XLI. praises and worships Ahura Mazda and Righteousness the Best. It asks for Ahura Mazda’s good Kingdom, long life, power, salvation, protection, and reward, and concludes with a sacrifice to Yasna Haptanghâiti.

Ahura Mazda is praised as the King, the Life, and the Rewarder. He is asked to rule benevolently, grant life and bodily vigor, give power and salvation, protect the worshippers, and bestow the reward appointed for souls.
Righteousness the Best is praised and worshipped alongside Ahura Mazda. Its protecting guardianship is sought for ever.
Ahura Mazda's good Kingdom is something the worshippers seek to attain for ever. They ask that Ahura Mazda be a good King over them.
Long life is sought from Ahura Mazda. The worshippers ask to win and conquer it through his grace and to receive his help.

l: sacred reward and blessing, Yasna, Yasna XLI.
s: The reward appointed for the souls is associated with what is most meet for their deserving. The worshippers ask Ahura Mazda to bestow it for this life and for that of mind, together with protecting guardianship.
Yasna Haptanghâiti is offered sacrifice as a brave Yasna. It is described as holy and as the ritual chief.

The text worships the Bountiful Immortals through the entire collection of the Yasna, Haptanghâiti. It offers sacrifices to waters, rivers, roads, hills, lakes, corn, earth, heaven, the stormy wind Mazda made, Haraiti, and other good things. It also honors Zarathustra, the Lord, the Good Mind in the living, spirits of the saints, Vouru-kasha, and various sacred beings. Haoma is praised as golden-flowered, restorative, helpful to the world's advance, and able to drive death away.
The Bountiful Immortals are worshipped with the entire collection of the Yasna, Haptanghâiti. Sacrifice is also offered to all the Bountiful Immortals.
The Yasna is presented as the collection through which the Bountiful Immortals are worshipped.
Haptanghâiti is identified as the collection, or portion of the Yasna, used in worship of the Bountiful Immortals.
Zarathustra is included among those to whom sacrifice is offered, together with the Lord.
The Lord is included among those to whom sacrifice is offered, together with Zarathustra.
Mazda made the stormy wind, which is included among the things to which sacrifice is offered.
The Good Mind is worshipped in the living.
Vouru-kasha contains the sea where the sacred Unicorn (?) stands. Sacrifice is offered to that sea.
Haoma is described as golden-flowered and growing on the heights. It restores, aids the world's advance, and drives death afar; sacrifice is offered to it.

Yasna XLIII concerns Zarathustra’s reflections on Ahura Mazda’s bountifulness and the universal salvation offered to believers. Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda for Righteousness, Piety, the Good Mind, holy blessings, spiritual glory, and long life. Ahura Mazda’s messengers question and instruct Zarathustra, who pledges to oppose the wicked, help the righteous, and prepare people for Ahura Mazda’s Kingdom. The unit describes final judgment, the role of Âramaiti and Sraosha, and the blessings associated with Ahura Mazda’s Realm.

Ahura Mazda is portrayed as the Great Creator, living Lord, supreme ruler, and bountiful giver. He grants or reveals Righteousness, Piety, the Good Mind, spiritual glory, wisdom, holy blessings, and rewards according to deeds and words. He establishes evil for the evil and happy blessings for the good in the creation’s final change.

Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda for spiritual gifts, guidance, long life, and the ability to serve the righteous order. He declares that he would be a tormentor of the wicked and a help and joy to the righteous. He pledges to praise Ahura Mazda, prepare for His Kingdom, teach the true aims of human desires, and arouse the chiefs of the proclamation.

The Good Mind reveals Ahura Mazda’s thoughts of wisdom and approaches Zarathustra through a messenger. Its power comes to Zarathustra, and its grace accompanies Sraosha. Through the Good Mind, Âramaiti gives blessings in reward for deeds.

Righteousness is sought by Zarathustra as a sustaining and indwelling power. Through it, Ahura Mazda’s aids and Fire’s flame become strong, settlements are furthered, and rewards are assigned. Zarathustra prays that Righteousness will be life-strong and clothed with body.

Âramaiti is identified with Piety within the worshipper and is asked to grant holy blessings and perfect readiness of mind. She utters saving regulations and Ahura Mazda’s understanding, and she is present in the holy Realm to give blessings through the Good Mind.

Sraosha is identified with Obedience and approaches Zarathustra with the Good Mind. Sraosha questions him, instructs him to let the quiet and better mind teach him, and is asked to accompany him with holy recompense and spiritual splendour.
Salvation is announced for this man and for whosoever may be. It is connected with the gifts of Ahura Mazda, the maintenance of Righteousness, and the blessings granted to the righteous.

Ahura Mazda’s Realm is the desired place declared to be within His domain. It is associated with the preparation of Ahura Mazda’s Kingdom and is described as a holy Realm that shines with splendour like the sun.

Fire’s flame is described as strong through the Holy Order and as receiving an offering of praise and holiness from Zarathustra. Zarathustra desires to meditate on this offering and plan for its holy power among Ahura Mazda’s people.

Ahura Mazda’s bounteous spirit is associated with sovereign power, gifts, and the granting of spiritual glory. Zarathustra says he loves the Spirit, and spiritual gifts are to be given to contending throngs as blessings of certainty and peace.

The speaker asks Ahura Mazda to explain the origins and workings of creation, including the Righteous Order, the sun, stars, moon, earth, waters, plants, winds, lights, darkness, sleep, and dawns. The speaker seeks instruction on serving Ahura Mazda, increasing goodness, hallowing the Faith of Ahura Mazda's people, and attaining perfection, Welfare, and Immortality. The speaker asks how the Righteous Order and Good Mind will prevail over the Demon-of-the-Lie and its followers when the two hosts meet. The unit contrasts the friends and worshippers of Righteousness with Daêva-worshippers, Karpan, Usig, and the Kavian, who are associated with rapine and failure to bring waters and blessings to the fields.

Ahura Mazda is asked to explain creation, the Righteous Order, the Good Mind, and the proper way to serve Him. The speaker asks Ahura Mazda for protection, guidance, judgment between the two hosts, and gifts associated with Welfare and Immortality.

The speaker repeatedly asks Ahura Mazda to tell him aright about creation, worship, righteousness, wickedness, and the fate of opposing forces. He identifies himself as Ahura Mazda's foremost servant and asks how to increase in goodness, attain perfection, and receive protection and blessing.

The Righteous Order is presented as active within the world and within souls, sustaining right actions and governing the proper order of creation. It is associated with Ahura Mazda's protection, the Good Mind, the speaker's desired chieftainship, and judgment against the Demon-of-the-Lie.

The Good Mind is described as being within souls and as inspiring good thoughts, guiding questions, and helping one draw near to Ahura Mazda. Through it, the speaker seeks friendly help, the Realm, obedience to a worthy leader, and the perfection of life.

Piety Âramaiti is asked about as a force that increases sacred orderliness and makes actions just. She is described as beloved and connected with Ahura Mazda's Sovereign Power, the Faith, and the speaker's growth in goodness.

The Faith of Ahura Mazda's people is something the speaker seeks to hallow and understand. It is taught by the beneficent kingdom's lord and is said to advance the speaker's lands in Asha and make actions just through Piety Âramaiti.

The Demon-of-the-Lie is treated as a rebellious and harmful opponent whose influence gives no light to the friends of Righteousness. The speaker asks how to banish her, deliver her into the hands of the Righteous Order, cast her down to death through doctrine, and destroy her evil believers.

l: people devoted to Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna XLIV.
s: The worshippers of Ahura Mazda are associated with the Faith, Piety, Righteousness, and the Good Mind. The speaker asks how Piety may again approach them and how they may receive protection, guidance, and the blessings of Welfare and Immortality.

The Daêva-worshippers are questioned as to whether they have ever ruled as worthy kings. They are associated with fighting for those who act amiss, with the Karpan and Usig giving the Kine to Rapine, and with failing to bring waters to the fields for the Righteous Order.

Yasna XLV, titled the Doctrine of Dualism, concerns the declaration of Ahura Mazda’s teaching and the opposition between the two first spirits. It presents Ahura Mazda as the all-wise Lord and creator who establishes Righteousness, Good Mind, Piety, Weal, Immortality, and royal power. It teaches that the two spirits differ in thoughts, commands, beliefs, deeds, consciences, and souls, and that obedience to the Mãthra brings blessing while wickedness brings woe. It also condemns the Daêva-gods and describes the Saoshyant’s bounteous Faith as saving and beneficent.
Yasna XLV declares the Doctrine of Dualism and presents teachings concerning Ahura Mazda, the two first spirits, obedience, righteousness, and the consequences for the righteous and the wicked.

l: The Doctrine of Dualism, Yasna, Yasna XLV.
s: The Doctrine of Dualism teaches that the two first spirits are opposed in their thoughts, commands, understandings, beliefs, deeds, consciences, and souls.

Ahura Mazda is presented as the all-wise Lord, creator, father of the Good Mind, establisher of Righteousness, and giver of Weal and Immortality. He is praised and sought through Righteousness, Good Mind, and Piety, and is said to grant royal power and saving support.

l: two first spirits, Yasna, Yasna XLV.
s: The two first spirits are declared to differ from one another in thoughts, commands, understandings, beliefs, deeds, consciences, and souls. The more bountiful spirit speaks to the harmful spirit.
The Mãthra is the teaching that the speaker declares from Ahura Mazda. Those who do not fulfil and obey it are said to meet the end of life in woe.

Righteousness is associated with Mazda, who appoints what is true, and with the speaker’s knowledge and praise of Ahura Mazda. Through Righteousness, Ahura Mazda establishes blessings and supports the Good Mind.
The Good Mind is described as toiling within, born through Righteousness, and associated with Ahura Mazda’s support, wisdom, deeds, and kingdom. It is used to honour and seek Ahura Mazda.
Piety is described as the daughter of Ahura Mazda through good deeds. Yasnas of Piety are used to praise Ahura Mazda with homage.
Weal is a blessing that comes to those who give obedient attention to Ahura Mazda’s declared word. Ahura Mazda establishes it together with Immortality.
Immortality is granted with Weal to those who heed Ahura Mazda’s teaching. It is also desired by the souls of the righteous in eternal existence.
The righteous seek blessings, Weal, and Immortality, while their souls desire these in eternal Immortality. Their blessings contrast with the woes established for the wicked.
The Daêva-gods are described as having been despised, along with alien men, because they had held Ahura Mazda in derision.
The Saoshyant is associated with bounteous Faith and saving power. The Saoshyant is described as a friend, brother, or father to those addressed.

Zarathustra describes his lack of allies, reduced flocks, and need for help in establishing the Faith. He appeals to Ahura Mazda for guidance, protection, and the wealth of the Good Mind, while condemning evil rulers who obstruct the Righteous Order and harm the settlements. He asks for righteous judges and helpers, naming Kavi Vîstâspa, Frashaostra Hvôgva, Gâmâspa Hvôgva, and others who may advance the cause. He teaches that the righteous will receive blessings, while the wicked will fall into misery and the abode of the Lie.

Zarathustra seeks help in establishing the Faith and appeals to Ahura Mazda for guidance, protection, and the Good Mind's wealth. He names Kavi Vîstâspa as a heroic supporter and calls upon other allies to advance the Righteous Order.

Ahura Mazda is appealed to as Lord, commander, exhorter, and protector. He is asked to grant the Good Mind, defend the righteous, punish oppressors, and give joyful grace and commands to those who further the settlements of Piety.
The Good Mind is sought as spiritual wealth, guidance, and a means of advancing the Faith and Righteous Order. Ahura Mazda dwells with those who further the settlements through the Good Mind.
The Righteous Order is to be held upright, nurtured, and established through lawful and righteous action. Its supporters advance the settlements, while evil rulers obstruct its progress.
Zarathustra seeks to establish and maintain the Faith with Ahura Mazda's grace and the Good Mind. Its truths are to be declared, and its supporters are called to advance it.
Kavi Vîstâspa is named by Zarathustra as a heroic holy friend suited to support the great cause. Zarathustra intends to call him and others to the attempt with the Good Mind's words.
The Kine are associated with the sacred cause, the Righteous Order, and the blessings gained through the sacred mother-kine. Wisdom and rewards are sought for their welfare.
The settlements are endangered by evil rulers and may be delivered to harm. Those who further the settlements of Piety with energy and zeal receive Ahura Mazda's presence and joyful grace.
The Judge's Bridge is the place toward which Zarathustra will lead the righteous with those who follow him. The wicked approach it but miss their path and fall into the Lie's abode.

l: abode of the Lie, Yasna, Yasna XLVI.
s: The abode of the Lie is the everlasting habitation of the Karpan and Kavi who join in governments to destroy human life with evil deeds. Those who miss the path at the Judge's Bridge fall there.
The Lie is associated with evil rulers, wicked deeds, and the abode where the wicked remain forever. A person who fails to oppose an evil wrongdoer is said to go to the abode of the Lie.

This unit concerns Ahura Mazda’s gifts to His chosen saint through His Bountiful Spirit, Best Mind, Righteous moral Order, Sovereign Power, and Âramaiti. The gifts include Universal Weal and Immortality, brought forth through Good Mind, Âramaiti, and Fire. Ahura Mazda is described as the father of the righteous Order and the maker of the joy-creating Kine. The wicked foemen are harmed and remain aligned with the Evil Mind, while Piety and righteous Truth instruct those who seek them.

Ahura Mazda gives His chosen saint Universal Weal and Immortality through His Bountiful Spirit, Best Mind, Righteous moral Order, and Sovereign Power. He brings blessedness into action through Good Mind, Âramaiti, and Fire, is called the father of the righteous Order, and made the joy-creating Kine.

l: man (Ahura Mazda's chosen saint), Yasna, Yasna XLVII.
s: The chosen saint receives Universal Weal and Immortality, along with whatever is best, through Ahura Mazda’s Bountiful Spirit. He is associated with Good Mind and receives support from the feeble man, while the wicked ruler’s pride may slight him.

l: the Universal Weal, Yasna, Yasna XLVII.
s: Universal Weal is one of the two greatest gifts that Ahura Mazda gives to His chosen saint through His Bountiful Spirit.
Immortality is one of the two greatest gifts that Ahura Mazda gives to His chosen saint through His Bountiful Spirit.

Ahura Mazda’s Bountiful Spirit is the means by which He gives Universal Weal, Immortality, and other best gifts to His chosen saint. It brings blessedness into action and harms the wicked, but not the saints.

Ahura Mazda’s Best Mind is associated with His giving of Universal Weal and Immortality and with the expression of blessedness through words. The chosen saint takes counsel with Good Mind for the benefit of the Kine.
The Righteous moral Order motivates Ahura Mazda’s gifts in word and deed. Ahura Mazda is described as its father, and its increase is joined with Piety and righteous ritual and moral Truth.

Âramaiti brings forth blessedness through her two hands and is identified with Piety as she lives within the soul and as earth. Ahura Mazda bestows her as joyful meadows of peace for the Kine, and her increase helps instruct those who seek her.
The Kine is the joy-creating Kine made by Ahura Mazda. Ahura Mazda bestows Âramaiti as her joyful meadows of peace because the chosen saint has taken counsel with Good Mind.

The wicked foemen are harmed by Ahura Mazda’s Bountiful Spirit and receive their portion far from His love. They remain in the actions of the Evil Mind, and the evil person with wealth and ruling power serves the wicked.
The saints are not harmed by Ahura Mazda’s Bountiful Spirit. The chosen saint receives Ahura Mazda’s best gifts, while a feeble man can give support to Ahura Mazda’s saint.
The Evil Mind is the sphere in which the wicked remain through their actions. The wicked person’s portion is far from Ahura Mazda’s love because of this alignment.
Ahura Mazda’s Fire gives the gifts to the two striving throngs in a good bestowal. Its action accompanies the prosperous increase of Piety and Righteous moral Order.

Piety is represented by Âramaiti and is linked with peace for the Kine, the increase of righteous Truth, and the instruction of those who seek her. Its prosperous increase accompanies the gifts given through Ahura Mazda’s Bountiful Spirit and Fire.

The unit concerns prayers to Ahura Mazda for victory of the Righteous Order over the Demon-of-the-Lie, evil heretics, rapine, envy, and oppressive rulers. It asks for strength in conflicts, the rule of good kings, prosperity for the Kine, and refuge for the faithful. It looks toward the future appearance of the Saoshyant, perfected Piety, men of mind's perfection, and Saviours of the Provinces, who will advance the Holy Order through the Good Mind.

Ahura Mazda is asked to reveal the outcome of coming conflicts, grant strength and courage, establish good rule, and provide victory, reward, and blessing. He is associated with the Good Mind, the Righteous Order, the generation of primeval life, and the flourishing of plants for the Kine.

The Righteous Order is the basis for offerings, conflict against the Demon-of-the-Lie, holy teaching, rule, protection, and the saving work of the faithful. Its champions and Saviours act in accordance with it.
The Demon-of-the-Lie is identified as the inspiring spirit of the foes. The faithful hope that it will be smitten through action in accordance with the Righteous Order.

l: champion of the holy Order, Yasna, Yasna XLVIII.
s: The champion of the holy Order is expected to smite the evil heretic. The text asks when this victory will come and calls it the good consummation of life.

The enlightened man receives the best teachings proclaimed by Ahura Mazda through the Righteous Order and secret sayings declared in His name. He must follow the holy Faith and pursue what is better and more holy in word and action.

The Good Mind provides understanding, discernment, longing, grace, and sacred wisdom. Its deeds guide the faithful, support the Kine, and enable the Saviours of the Provinces to carry out Ahura Mazda's commandments.
The holy Faith is to be followed closely by the enlightened man, whose struggle and effort are devoted to it. His will, wish, creed, fealty, words, and actions must be consistent with it.
Âramaiti is addressed as pious wisdom and is asked to sanctify the best blessings for offspring. She is asked to help the Kine prosper and to support good rule through deeds of good discernment.
The Kine are to receive toil and care so that they prosper for human life. They grant pleasing homes and lasting strength, and plants are caused to flourish for their nurture.
